case_title: Badal Murmu and Ors. v. State of West Bengal
accused_socioeconomic_status: Very poor; described as economically weak tribals living in a very poor stratum of society
accused_victim_relationship: Prior enmity/dispute: the victim had stolen a hen belonging to one accused, leading to an inimical relation and a panchayat penalty
statutory_provisions: IPC s.148; IPC s.302 r/w s.149 (charged and tried); conviction altered to IPC s.304 Part II
weapon: Lathis (used); tangies (sharp cutting weapons) carried but not used
evidence_type: Eyewitness (PW-1, PW-3, PW-6, PW-7 including injured witness); medical (post-mortem by PW-9); police statement of first wife
aggravating_circumstances: Fourteen injuries including two rib fractures and haematoma under the scalp; victim tied up before the assault; beaten to death
mitigating_circumstances: Trivial underlying dispute over a stolen hen; no common object to kill shown; sharp weapons available but not used; accused poor tribals; long period in jail (almost 14 years)
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under s.148 and s.302 r/w s.149 IPC; sentenced to life imprisonment
high_court_outcome: Appeal dismissed; conviction and sentence confirmed
offence_finally_established: Culpable homicide not amounting to murder, IPC s.304 Part II
neutral_facts: A dispute arose after the victim allegedly stole a hen belonging to one of the accused. A community settlement was held and the victim paid a penalty, but the accused were reportedly still unhappy with it. Shortly afterwards, one accused allegedly confronted a witness about the matter and caused bleeding injuries to him, and the witness was examined by a doctor. On the following morning, the victim and this witness were summoned to a courtyard on the pretext of a meeting. On arrival, they were tied to a bamboo pole and a tree. Several accused, armed with lathis and tangies (sharp cutting weapons), allegedly beat the victim with lathis while the witness escaped. The victim was beaten to death. The victim's two wives, who had followed him to the courtyard, witnessed the assault. The first wife gave a statement to the police naming all accused as the assailants, and an investigation followed. The post-mortem doctor recorded fourteen injuries, mostly bruises and abrasions, including two rib fractures and haematoma under the scalp, stated that all injuries contributed to death, and said a blunt object such as a lathi could cause them. The witness, who was related to the victim, named his brother among the assailants. No witness attributed specific blows to specific accused, and the tangies were not used.
physical_harm: Death of the victim; fourteen injuries, mostly bruises and abrasions, plus two rib fractures and haematoma under the scalp
number_of_offences: 2 charged (s.148 and s.302 r/w s.149); 1 finally upheld (s.304 Part II substituted for s.302 r/w s.149; s.148 not separately addressed in Supreme Court)
financial_property_loss: Not applicable (the hen and liquor were a earlier panchayat penalty, not a loss from this offence)
premeditation_planning: Not found; the court held there was no shared common object to kill and the beating arose from a frenzy
motive: Anger over the theft of a hen and the panchayat penalty (court's view)
key_evidence_accepted: Ocular testimony of PW-1, PW-3, PW-6 and PW-7 that the accused assaulted the victim with lathis; post-mortem evidence of PW-9 that the injuries could be caused by a lathi
witness_credibility: Found truthful and having a ring of truth; related to the victim but not shown to have falsely implicated the accused; PW-7 named his own brother as an assailant
post_offence_conduct: Not stated (the quoted conduct concerns PW-7, not the accused)
trial_duration: offence: not given (quarrel on 14/4/1989; assault the following morning); trial judgment: not given; High Court: 20.01.2003; Supreme Court: 5 February 2014
legal_representation: Appellants: Vibha Datta Makhija (learned amicus) and Ruchi Agnihotri. State: Anip Sachthey, Kabir S. Bose, Shagun Matta and Saakaar Sardana
investigation_status: Statement given to Memari Police Station; investigation completed; accused charged and tried
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted under s.148 and s.302 r/w s.149 and sentenced to life imprisonment. High Court: appeal dismissed, conviction and sentence affirmed. Supreme Court: conviction under s.302 r/w s.149 set aside; convicted under s.304 Part II with sentence of time already undergone
prosecution_argument: Ocular evidence established the case; even if the common object was only to inflict injuries, members of the unlawful assembly knew murder was likely, so all are guilty of murder under s.149
defence_argument: Prosecution not proved beyond reasonable doubt; alternatively, guilt should be only culpable homicide not amounting to murder under s.304 Part II because there was no intention to kill, injuries were superficial, and the accused are poor tribals long in jail
legal_principle_applied: Common object under s.149 must be shown in the peculiar facts; where no individual role or fatal injury is attributed and no intent to kill is shown, murder conviction cannot be sustained and s.304 Part II applies
precedent_relied_upon: Kirti Mahto & Ors. v. State of Bihar 1994 Supp. (2) SCC 569; Molu & Ors. v. State of Haryana AIR 1976 SC 2499; Munivel v. State of Tamil Nadu (2006) 9 SCC 394; Alister Anthony Pareira v. State of Maharashtra (2012) 2 SCC 648; Kashmiri Lal & Ors. v. State of Punjab AIR 1997 SC 393; Sukhdev Singh v. State of Punjab AIR 1992 SC 755; Sarman & Ors. v. State of Madhya Pradesh 1993 Supp. (2) SCC 356
sentencing_rationale: Trivial triggering incident; no shared intent to kill; accused's economic and social background; nearly 14 years already in jail; sentence of time undergone under s.304 Part II meets ends of justice
judicial_mitigating_factors: Background of economic and social status; trivial cause of the incident; no shared common object to kill; sharp weapons not used; almost 14 years in jail
other_sentence_order: Accused directed to be released forthwith unless required in any other case

case_title.quote: BADAL MURMU AND ORS. V. STATE OF WEST BENGAL

accused_caste.quote: The appellants and the prosecution witnesses belong to Santhal Community of village Mobarakpur.

accused_socioeconomic_status.quote: They come from a very poor strata of the society and appear to be untouched by the effect of urbanization.

victim_gender.quote: PW-1 Nilmoni, the first wife of deceased-Jhore Soren narrated the entire incident after describing the previous incident about the stealing of the hen by her husband

victim_caste.quote: The appellants and the prosecution witnesses belong to Santhal Community of village Mobarakpur.

accused_victim_relationship.quote: there was inimical relation between the deceased and accused family due to stealing of hen of one appellant-8 by the deceased.

offence_category.quote: They were convicted for offences punishable under Section 148 and Section 302 read with Section 149 of the IPC

statutory_provisions.quote: They were convicted for offences punishable under Section 148 and Section 302 read with Section 149 of the IPC

weapon.quote: The appellants were armed with lathis, tangies (sharp cutting weapons) etc.

evidence_type.quote: PW-9 Dr. Prodip Kumar, who did the post-mortem of deceased-Jhore Soren stated that the death was caused due to the injuries described by him

aggravating_circumstances.quote: It is true that the doctor noticed fourteen injuries on the deceased.

mitigating_circumstances.quote: It is an unusual case where a trivial incident led to a murder.

trial_court_outcome.quote: they were convicted for offences punishable under Section 148 and Section 302 read with Section 149 of the IPC and sentenced to undergo imprisonment for life for causing death of one Jhore Soren

high_court_outcome.quote: The appellants' appeal was dismissed by the High Court.

final_outcome.quote: the conviction of the appellants for offences punishable under Section 302 read with Section 149 of the IPC is quashed and set aside.

offence_finally_established.quote: convicting the appellants for culpable homicide not amounting to murder and sentencing them for the period already undergone by them

imprisonment_type.quote: sentencing them for the period already undergone by them by resorting to Section 304 Part II of the IPC

neutral_facts.quote: On the next day, in the morning, deceased-Jhore Soren and PW-7 Kanka were called. to the courtyard of one Saheb Hasda on the pretext that a meeting was to be held over the previous day's incident.

attempt_completion.quote: The appellants continued to beat deceased Jhore Soren. He was beaten to death.

physical_harm.quote: It is true that the doctor noticed fourteen injuries on the deceased. Most of them were bruises and abrasions.

number_of_offences.quote: the conviction of the appellants for offences punishable under Section 302 read with Section 149 of the IPC is quashed and set aside.

financial_property_loss.quote: He was ordered to give a hen to appellant Bhagbat and, in addition, he had to give two handies of liquor.

premeditation_planning.quote: the attendant circumstances do not indicate that the appellants shared any common object to kill deceased-Jhore Soren.

motive.quote: their anger and reaction to the theft of hen must be viewed against the background of their economic and social status.

key_evidence_accepted.quote: The evidence of PW-1 Nilmoni, PW-3 Rabi Soren, PW-6 Sumi Soren and PW-7 Kanka is truthful and has rightly been relied upon.

witness_credibility.quote: They are rustic witnesses and have candidly stated all that they had seen.

post_offence_conduct.quote: His evidence indicates that out of fear he ran away and did not inform anyone about the incident.

custody_duration.quote: we are informed that the appellants are in jail for almost 14 years.

trial_duration.quote: From the Judgment and Order dated 20.01.2003 of the High Court at Calcutta

legal_representation.quote: Vibha Datta Makhija, Ruchi Agnihotri for the Appellants.

investigation_status.quote: upon completion of the investigation, the appellants came to be charged as aforesaid.

appeal_history.quote: The High Court affirmed the same.

prosecution_argument.quote: since death was caused, every member of the unlawful assembly must be held guilty of murder.

defence_argument.quote: the prosecution has failed to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt and, therefore, the appellants deserve to be acquitted.

legal_principle_applied.quote: the doctor has not stated which injury was fatal. It is difficult therefore to say that all the appellants are guilty of murder.

sentencing_rationale.quote: Apart from the legal angle, this, in our view, is a case where justice must be tempered with mercy.

judicial_mitigating_factors.quote: Though, there can be no justification for the appellants' actions, their anger and reaction to the theft of hen must be viewed against the background of their economic and social status.

other_sentence_order.quote: They are directed to be released forthwith unless they are otherwise required in any other case.
